summary: [Tech Debt] ExhibitorEffectiveSettings: make category-less / AccountEvent-less exhibitors safe by construction (retire the $resolvable hotfix)

ai.s: Makes exhibitor effective settings safe for exhibitors with no category or no owner event row, replacing the partial $resolvable hotfix.
ai.pr: ExhibitorEffectiveSettings threw an HTTP 500 for category-less or AccountEvent-less exhibitors; the EP-55072 hotfix guarded only the logo gate, leaving 13 other methods exposed.
ai.wy: Requested as tech debt on EP-55072 to close the whole bug group; these states keep arising in production, e.g. from event deletion.
ai.oc: Settings resolution is to handle missing category or owner rows by construction, so none of the public methods can 500 on them.

summary: Admin Panel/ Add Purchase History for Lead Capture Pro & Add-ons to Exhibitor Profile

ai.s: Adds a Purchase History section to the admin exhibitor profile showing Lead Capture Pro and add-on purchases with their transaction status.
ai.pr: The admin panel gave no visibility of whether an exhibitor had bought Lead Capture Pro or add-ons such as AI Notetaker, nor of the transaction status.
ai.wy: Support and account teams could not verify client purchase claims without escalating or digging through billing systems.
ai.oc: The section is to show purchases, add-ons, dates, status (successful, pending, failed, refunded) and ideally a transaction reference.

summary: Remove unused Lead Capture Pro purchase-page view analytics (EP-54359)

ai.s: Removes the unused Lead Capture Pro purchase-page view analytics added in EP-54359.
ai.pr: The LEAD_CAPTURE_PRO_VIEW tracking never saved any data, and the product owner withdrew the requirement.
ai.wy: Dead code clean-up after a withdrawn requirement.
ai.oc: The event dispatch, subscriber mapping, enum value, statistics classes and test are to be deleted so no reference remains.

summary: Alphabetical Sorting for Filter Items for sessions and Exhibitor Events

ai.s: Sorts filter items alphabetically for sessions and exhibitor events (detail is in a linked Confluence page only).
ai.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumably filter items were not listed alphabetically.
ai.wy: Reported by HINTE; not otherwise specified.
ai.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; rough estimates only (BE 6 days, FE 2, QA 4).

summary: DS: analyse the whole prod-failed backlog in backup_events — only meeting create is covered today

ai.s: Analyses the full backlog of statistics events silently discarded by the pipeline, beyond the meeting-create slice already covered.
ai.pr: The statistics lambda drops events whose dictionary lookup fails, marking them prod-failed in backup_events with no alert, and the scale goes far beyond meeting create.
ai.wy: Found while repairing EP-55083 meeting data; client analytics may be losing many other event types.
ai.oc: The whole prod-failed backlog is to be sized and characterised by event type so each loss can be traced and repaired.

summary: Include exhibitor events in sessions page

ai.s: Makes the mobile app's Sessions list and calendar view honour the organiser's "Include Exhibitor Events in Sessions" setting.
ai.pr: It was unconfirmed whether the app showed exhibitor events alongside sessions in both the list and calendar views when the setting was on, as web does.
ai.wy: Attendees should see one unified agenda across web and app.
ai.oc: Both app surfaces are to consume the same setting that governs web, listing exhibitor events with regular sessions when enabled.

summary: Location Filter for Sessions and Exhibitor Events (Web)

epic.summary: New filters for Sessions and Exhibitor events

ai.s: Adds a location filter for sessions and exhibitor events on web (detail is in a linked Confluence page only).
ai.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title and epic (New filters for Sessions and Exhibitor events).
ai.wy: Reported by HINTE; part of the new sessions and exhibitor events filters epic.
ai.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to let attendees filter sessions and exhibitor events by location.

summary: DS: continuous fix for meeting analytics — the broken events keep arriving until every app is updated

ai.s: Sets up a continuous repair for meeting analytics, since old app versions will keep sending broken meeting events until every user updates.
ai.pr: Three app defects lose or misattribute meeting events at source, including 99% of iOS exhibitor-type meeting creates on IMEX event 1295, and a store release does not stop old versions.
ai.wy: A one-off migration cannot fix data that keeps arriving broken for months.
ai.oc: A mechanism building on the prod-failed detector is to repair incoming events continuously until the error rate reaches zero.

summary: account_events_dictionary PG view reports exhibitor owners as opted out — align it with the owner exemption the ClickHouse dictionaries apply

ai.s: Aligns the account_events_dictionary Postgres view with ClickHouse so exhibitor owners are no longer reported as opted out of networking.
ai.pr: The view computed consent from the raw gdpr_accept checkbox only, so owners with it unticked showed as opted out, unlike every other consent consumer.
ai.wy: One field had two definitions, giving inconsistent consent data across systems.
ai.oc: The view is to apply the same owner exemption as the ClickHouse dictionaries.

summary: redirectToSignInIfNeeded loses the return URL when bouncing to /signin

ai.s: Keeps the return URL when unauthenticated users are sent to sign-in from a protected layout, so they land back on the page they opened.
ai.pr: redirectToSignInIfNeeded sent users to a bare /signin with no return path, and the sign-in page never read one, so deep links were lost.
ai.wy: Shared links to protected exhibitor or session pages should work after sign-in.
ai.oc: The layout guard is to pass the original destination via the existing goto convention and sign-in is to honour it.

summary: Mobile apps still emit exhibitor favourite/unfavourite/view through the legacy POST /app/statistics/setActions — move them to the statistics WebSocket the apps already use for everything else

ai.s: Moves the mobile apps' exhibitor favourite, unfavourite and view statistics from the legacy setActions REST route to the statistics WebSocket.
ai.pr: Current iOS and Android builds sent exhibitor interactions through legacy POST /app/statistics/setActions while all other statistics went over WebSocket.
ai.wy: Unify statistics ingestion and retire the legacy route, which still carried live traffic across tenants.
ai.oc: The three exhibitor actions are to be emitted over the existing WebSocket channel and the legacy route dropped.

summary: Migrate remaining require-sign-in navigation (JoinButtonInterface, session registration) off the dead callBackFunction to the goto convention

ai.s: Moves the remaining require-sign-in navigation for session join and registration off a dead callback to the goto convention, so it works after login.
ai.pr: JoinButtonInterface and useSchedule relied on a callBackFunction that was never stored or read, so post-login navigation never ran.
ai.wy: Same root cause as EP-56255; users were not taken to registration or the session room after signing in.
ai.oc: Navigation branches are to use the goto query parameter, with business actions handled separately.

summary: US-1: Access via unique email link (v1)

ai.s: Exhibitors can open the ExpoIntelligence insights portal from a tokenised email link without an ExpoPlatform login.
ai.pr: Exhibitors had no login-free way to reach their insights portal.
ai.wy: Foundation for the Exhibitor Insights Portal, delivered through email campaigns.
ai.oc: A token scoped to one exhibitor and event with expiry, revocation and read-only access is specified; delivery and revocation ownership are still undefined.

summary: US-2: Solo exhibitor view

ai.s: A solo exhibitor lands directly on their own guided journey and full insights report in the ExpoIntelligence portal.
ai.pr: There was no insights view for an exhibitor without child stands.
ai.wy: Core use case of the Exhibitor Insights Portal.
ai.oc: All 7 sections are to populate from live data scoped to the exhibitor, with no stand switcher; sizing awaits metric definitions and spike EP-56324.

summary: US-3: Stand summary (parent + children)

ai.s: Parent exhibitors see a Stand Summary aggregating their own and all child exhibitors' KPIs in the insights portal.
ai.pr: Parent exhibitors had no combined view of leads, meetings, views, favourites and messages across their stand.
ai.wy: Exhibitors with sub-exhibitors need a stand-level picture.
ai.oc: Summed and deduplicated KPIs with a combined benchmark are specified; blocked on the dedup rule for buyers who met several children.

summary: US-4: Child switcher

ai.s: Parent exhibitors can switch from the Stand Summary into any individual child exhibitor's insights report.
ai.pr: There was no way for a parent to drill from the stand view into each exhibitor's own report.
ai.wy: Part of the Exhibitor Insights Portal parent/child experience.
ai.oc: A switcher listing parent and children is specified, with one-click return and children unable to see siblings; depends on US-3.

summary: US-5: White-label branding

ai.s: The insights portal carries the event's own logo on the gate, report header and exports, falling back to the ExpoPlatform mark.
ai.pr: The portal had no event branding.
ai.wy: The portal should look like the organiser's product to its exhibitors.
ai.oc: The event logo is to be pulled from Admin → General → Logo via the Event API; flagged as the lowest-risk story for early pickup.

summary: US-6: Guided journey + one-page report

ai.s: Builds the insights portal's guided journey and one-page report, with 12 insight cards over 7 sections and Excel/PDF export.
ai.pr: The approved prototype showed only hardcoded mock numbers with no metric definitions or data sources.
ai.wy: Deliver parity with the approved ExpoIntelligence prototype.
ai.oc: Every number is to trace to a defined metric query and exports include all unlocked sections; blocked on ~40 metric definitions.

summary: US-7: Benchmarks vs similar exhibitors

ai.s: Shows exhibitors their percentile position against an anonymised peer cohort from the same event.
ai.pr: Exhibitors had no benchmark against similar exhibitors.
ai.wy: Benchmarks give exhibitors context for their event performance.
ai.oc: Cohorts of at least 8 with non-identifiable peers are specified; blocked on Legal anonymity sign-off and an undefined cohort definition.

summary: US-8: Buyer interaction insights

ai.s: Shows exhibitors which buyers viewed, favourited, searched, messaged or met them, with profile context.
ai.pr: Exhibitors could not see buyer interactions in one insights view.
ai.wy: Buyer insight is a core value of the Exhibitor Insights Portal.
ai.oc: Listing only interacting buyers within lead-sharing rules is specified; blocked on undefined lead-sharing rules and buyer interaction coverage gaps.
